segments.title: Chương 5: 0005【Hịch văn và Cyberpunk】
segments.content:
The three returned to their dorm.

In the room, only Liu Zhihong and Yang Hao were playing chess.

Xie Yang shoved his battered suitcase under the bed and asked his two chess-playing roommates, "Where are the other three?"

"They went to the classroom to review," Liu Zhihong said, slamming a chess piece down. "Checkmate by cannon after horse, check!"

Yang Hao was so anxious he was scratching his head.

Liu Zhihong sat on the edge of the bed picking his feet, saying smugly, "Just hand over your rook for me to take."

Chen Guiliang stood to the side, observing the two of them.

In his memory, Liu Zhihong and Yang Hao were like missing persons; he had completely lost track of them after high school graduation.

After watching for a while, Chen Guiliang grabbed his clothes to take a shower. He felt sticky all over.

This crappy dormitory building had no private bathrooms. Each floor shared one toilet and one bathroom (which also served as a laundry room).

Naturally, there were no water heaters or bath heaters either. Students had to go to the boiler room to get hot water.

Chen Guiliang didn't even bother with hot water. He had taken cold showers for all three years of high school.

It was the same even when it snowed in the dead of winter.

Because hot water cost 2 mao per kettle, Chen Guiliang felt it was too much of a waste.

At this moment, someone was washing clothes in the bathroom and took the initiative to greet him, "Great Hero Chen, taking a shower!"

"How did the exam go today?" Chen Guiliang had forgotten who this person was, so he could only make small talk.

The person rubbed soap on their clothes and scrubbed vigorously, "It went alright."

Chen Guiliang placed his bucket on the washing sink and casually turned on the tap.

While the cold water was filling up, he stripped off his clothes and pants, and shook his magnificent johnson.

This is the kind of detail an author who's lacking would deliberately write. The classmate washing clothes happened to turn around and see it, and was immediately struck with a sense of inadequacy.

After filling the bucket most of the way, Chen Guiliang poured it over his head.

Tomorrow was the "Start of Winter." The sudden drenching of cold water was a truly invigorating sensation.

It had been almost twenty years since he had done this. Chen Guiliang found it quite interesting.

He hadn't even bought shampoo, just rubbing a bar of soap all over his head. After scrubbing his hair for a bit, the second bucket of cold water was already full.

Shivering, Chen Guiliang couldn't be bothered with the bucket this time and stuck his head directly under the faucet to rinse.

By the time he finished his shower, he was trembling all over.

It didn't matter if he caught a cold and ran a fever. He could tough it out without medicine.

Left-behind children from the countryside had humble lives, but they were also hardy. Like weeds growing from cracks in stone, sunlight and water were luxuries, but give them the slightest chance and they would survive.

Shoving his dirty clothes into the bucket, Chen Guiliang walked back to the dorm in his slippers.

There was no hairdryer.

His dripping wet hair was just left to air dry.

Xie Yang was lying on his bed reading *Zichuan*, while Xu Haibo was reviewing for tomorrow's liberal arts comprehensive exam.

Chen Guiliang took out a pen and paper, intending to write his submission for the competition.

Chen Guiliang was quite good at writing.

He had majored in journalism in university and interned at a major southern newspaper while still in school. After graduating, he covered social news and even worked as an undercover reporter for two years.

After one of his articles was maliciously altered by a copy editor to stir up social conflict, he resigned in anger and was introduced by a friend to work as an editor at a magazine.

But then he ran into the decline of the traditional media industry. After just half a year as an editor, the magazine went out of business.

Next, Chen Guiliang joined a web portal.

But that web portal was also on the decline. Left with no choice, Chen Guiliang jumped ship to a gaming company.

The gaming industry in those years was like a chaotic jungle, and those who performed well could get promoted with lightning speed. He first worked in the marketing department, then transferred to the operations department, and became the deputy director of operations in just three years.

The operations department of a gaming company seemed to hold great power on the surface, but in reality, it couldn't make decisions on anything. And whenever a problem arose, it had to take the blame for the R&D and marketing departments!

Having become a veteran scapegoat, Chen Guiliang was eventually fired by the boss for taking the fall for a major incident.

Middle-aged, unemployed, and divorced—a double blow.

Having hit rock bottom, Chen Guiliang took his marital assets and started a gaming company with three friends.

Full of ambition.

And lost every penny!

Just when they were at their wit's end, a friend who was a mid-level manager at Shanda asked if they needed an official license for *Legend*.

By paying Shanda 150,000 yuan a month, they could freely modify it into a web game or mobile game. They could even legally run private servers, as long as their version didn't get ahead of the official one.

Because they entered the *Legend* mobile game market relatively early, this scrappy game actually made them a fortune.

Next, they started making reskinned web and mobile games, specifically for the nouveau riche market in the Middle East—the "XX of Sudan" type.

All four shareholders, including Chen Guiliang, achieved financial freedom.

With success in business came internal strife.

There was a whole heap of bullshit, which angered Chen Guiliang so much that he just threw in the towel, deciding to cultivate his mind, rediscover his literary dream, and even went to Qidian to write two flop books.

In a fit of pique, he went to Qidian to write two entertainment industry novels, got banned, then switched to the history category. So, what should he write for the competition submission?

The preliminary screeners were all editors from *Mengya*.

They had too many manuscripts to read through, so he had to grab their attention right from the beginning of the article.

Chen Guiliang sat at his desk, thinking carefully, when his eyes suddenly fell on the contents of a newspaper. It was an old paper from six months ago, spread across the desk by the window as a tablecloth.

Front-page headline: America Invades Iraq!

Inspiration struck instantly.

Xu Haibo was sitting on the other side of the desk, originally reviewing for tomorrow's exam. Hearing Chen Guiliang writing furiously, he curiously got up and walked over to see.

The more he read, the more astonished he became, until he was utterly dumbfounded.

But he didn't dare interrupt Chen Guiliang's creative process. It was only after the article was finished that Xu Haibo suddenly shouted, "Everyone, come and see, Great Hero Chen's article is so fucking awesome!"

"What the hell are you on about."

Xie Yang, who was blissfully reading his novel, first cursed at Xu Haibo before slowly wandering over to read aloud:

"'A Denunciation of America's Invasion of Iraq.' The American chieftain, one George W. Bush, is by nature fierce and malicious, and in his conduct, brutish and violent. In the past, he relied on might to bully the weak; now, he engineers disaster to plague the people. He harbors a sinister heart for oil, and usurps the authority of the globe. He professes the name of freedom, yet nurses a rapacious greed..."

"'Iraq, that ancient land of two rivers, that olden nation of the Crescent... And yet, there are the cabal of clowns in the White House, fabricating false evidence of biochemical weapons, spreading fictitious claims of uranium bombs... A hundred thousand souls become new ghosts, a thousand years of civilization fall into the nine abysses...'"

"'In antiquity, King Zhou of Shang was a tyrant, and his army defected at Muye; the Nazis were rampant, and their heads were taken in Berlin. Today, the American empire's tyranny far surpasses that of Jie and Zhou, its cunning more deceitful than the Axis...'"

"'All who have red blood in their veins are filled with fury. Those who yet possess conscience, how can they sit idly by... The US dollar is stained with blood, and shall in the end devour itself; a crown woven of lies will surely fall into the filth. The setting sun on the White House already reveals the fading shadow of an empire; when the Stars and Stripes fall, we can await the coming of justice! Let this proclamation spread across the world, so that all may know.'"

This kind of article wasn't that rare.

Anyone with a decent foundation in classical Chinese could write one.

But in the eyes of a group of high school students, it was a breathtaking masterpiece for the ages.

After Xie Yang finished reading the article, he actually forgot to flip his hair to look cool. He stood stunned for a few seconds before saying, "Holy shit, how the hell did you write something so awesome?"

Liu Zhihong snatched the article to read it again, going over it twice before saying, "Son of a bitch, no wonder you always get full marks on your essays."

Yang Hao was more introverted. He racked his brain for a long time, then gave Chen Guiliang a thumbs-up and said, "Great Hero Chen wrote it so well, you'll definitely get first prize. You're practically the second Guo Xiaosi of our school!"

The second Guo Xiaosi...

Chen Guiliang found this very awkward, feeling as though he had just been insulted.

"I have to copy this down!" Xu Haibo's face was full of admiration, wishing he could take the article and show it to the whole school.

High school students were still relatively pure. As long as you had real talent, you could win their sincere respect.

Chen Guiliang ignored his roommates' compliments and sat there, starting to brainstorm his second submission.

He had bought four copies of *Mengya*, so he could cut out the submission pages and send in four different pieces.

It was best not to touch essays, especially those that went against mainstream thought.

Who knew what kind of people were among the editors.

Even the panel of famous writers who judged the finals were more or less influenced by neoliberalism.

It wouldn't be fair to say they were all rebels, but they had long been unconsciously influenced. The limitations of the era were there. Didn't even that little dog Yu praise Mo Sang's *Life and Death Are Wearing Me Out* as fucking awesome back then?

Chen Guiliang had no interest in getting into a war of words with them. He just wanted to get into a prestigious university through the New Concept Composition Competition.

A war of words would be useless, a waste of ink.

Chen Guiliang had worked in the southern media for a few years and knew all too well what those people were like. He himself had once been one of them. It was only after his article was maliciously altered that he came to his senses and quickly leaped out of that cesspool.

Wait until China's economy takes off and the West becomes a mess, and most people's views will naturally change.

Those who refuse to change can just be treated as rebels and given a good kick.

Chen Guiliang glanced at Xie Yang, who was on his internet detox, and picked up his pen to write his second submission: *My Cyber Homeland*.

This was a cyberpunk short story, only about 5,000 characters long, which could be expanded into a full-length novel at any time.

————

(Organizing a signature campaign to oppose the school is exciting, while carrying a shoulder pole of bamboo shoots into the city to sell is shameful. The two are very different, and these are both Lao Wang's personal experiences. It's a pity that when old classmates reunited more than a decade later, and the matter of the signature campaign to demand the return of the computer lab fee was brought up, most of them couldn't even remember it.)

(Many parts of the first hundred thousand words of this book are from Lao Wang's personal experiences, with the timeline deliberately moved forward by two or three years. Some parts were exaggerated for writing. Some were deliberately downplayed because reality was too outrageous to pass censorship.)

The johnson was exaggerated. (Thanks to the two great bosses, Zéxiān Qítiān and Xuányuán Qīnghuán, for the Alliance Leader tips.)
